Class JceDataKeyProvider

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.codec.crypto.JceDataKeyProvider
All Implemented Interfaces:
DataKeyProvider
public final class JceDataKeyProvider extends Object implements DataKeyProvider
In-process DataKeyProvider for consumers without a KMS, backed by one or more key-encryption keys (KEKs) supplied at construction.

The constructor takes a Map<String, SecretKey> of AES-256 KEKs keyed by id, plus the id of the current wrapping KEK. Generated data-encryption keys (DEKs) are AES-256, drawn from SecureRandom, and wrapped with AES key-wrap (AES/KW/NoPadding, RFC 3394): unlike GCM, AES-KW needs no nonce, so wrapping the same DEK under the same KEK always produces the same ciphertext, and its integrity check value (ICV) causes unwrap of a tampered or foreign-key blob to fail rather than silently return garbage key material.

The blob returned as DataKey.wrapped() is [scheme:1][wrapped key]: a one-byte wrap-scheme tag (WRAP_SCHEME_AES_KW, 0x01) followed by the AES-KW output — 41 bytes total for a 32-byte DEK. This is invisible to EnvelopeCodec, which treats the whole blob as opaque; it exists so this provider has the same wrap-algorithm migration story a KMS-backed provider gets from its own versioned ciphertext format. Scheme values 0x02 and above are reserved for future wrap algorithms; unwrap(String, byte[]) rejects any blob shorter than 2 bytes or tagged with an unrecognized scheme.

The KEK map is this provider's allowlist: allowsKeyId(String) and unwrap(String, byte[]) both consult it directly, so any key id absent from the map is rejected — this satisfies the DataKeyProvider security contract without any separate configuration. New data keys always wrap under the configured current KEK, while unwrap accepts any KEK present in the map; this asymmetry is what lets a consumer rotate KEKs by adding a new entry, pointing currentKeyId at it, and keeping the old entry only until every message wrapped under it has been re-encrypted.

The two public constructors cover the simple default case: a new SecureRandom instance, or a caller-supplied one as a test seam, with AES/KW/NoPadding resolved via the JDK's default provider lookup. Use builder(String, Map) instead when a Provider needs to be selected explicitly — for example a FIPS-validated provider pinned to this instance rather than installed globally; the builder also exposes the SecureRandom seam via secureRandom(SecureRandom).

    • allowsKeyId

      public boolean allowsKeyId(String keyId)
      Description copied from interface: DataKeyProvider
      Returns whether this provider is willing to unwrap data keys wrapped under the given key id.

      This is the provider's own admission check. The default implementation allows every key id; implementations backed by a fixed set of trusted keys (such as a Map of KEKs) should override this to reject any key id outside that set.

      Specified by:
      allowsKeyId in interface DataKeyProvider
      Parameters:
      keyId - the key id to evaluate
      Returns:
      true if this provider will unwrap data keys under keyId
